subject: How to write a nonstandard prior in Stan?

messages.author: 3b718630a63ab359
messages.subject: How to write a nonstandard prior in Stan?
parts:
I have a standard logistic regression model, with two predictors. So I have beta0, beta1 and beta2, each have a Normal prior. 

Then I calculate p[i] <- inv_logit(beta0 + beta1 * x1[i] + beta2 * x2[i]).

I want to add a binomial prior to the number of p[i] that are larger than a value, say, 0.5. I can write
lambda[i] <- int_step(p[i] - 0.5);
lambda_sum <- sum(lambda);
lambda_sum ~ binomial(n, theta);

But then Stan would give a non-fatal warning saying: Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression

I guess the way it's written is a little confusing. On one hand, lambda is calculated from p, which is calculated from beta's and data x. On the other hand, the binomial part tries to sample lambda_sum from the Binomial distribution. So I guess this may not be the right way of writing it.

any suggestions?

Thanks!!!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to write a nonstandard prior in Stan?
parts:
With the binomial formulation, the lambda[i] are independent
and you could just drop them altogether replace the step function with
a comparison, and write

(p[i] > 0.5) ~ bernoulli(theta);

You could even remove the inv_logit for p[i] and compare on the logit
scale:

for (i in 1:N)
(beta0 + beta1 * x1[i] + beta2 * x2[i] > logit(0.5)) ~ bernoulli(theta);

And you don't technically need a Jacobian here, but ...

Your bigger problem is that it's a non-continuous prior,
which HMC isn't really designed to handle. I doubt Gibbs will mix
any better. The samples will not mix well, especially if there are
a lot of cases near the boundary. And you may wind up with posterior
modes (my intuition's not good here as to what this prior's doing).

But I wouldn't recommend it. Reformulating the prior as something
continuous would be better, such as a prior on the expected number
of successes, which is just sum(p) in your formulation.

- Bob
